description: SIAGUAPY, the national system for sustainable water management of the Paraguayan Ministry of Environment, brings together hydrological data at national and river basin scale. Its monitoring pages list conventional and automatic stations on the Pilcomayo, Paraguay, Tebicuary and Yhaguy rivers and wells in the Patiño aquifer, with the latest level and a history for each, updated every 15 minutes from the APIs of the Directorate of Meteorology and Hydrology. The hydrological alerts page classes Paraguay River stations as normal, alert, critical or disaster by level, and tells pumping stations in the Tebicuary basin whether pumping can continue, must be staggered or must stop. The national water inventory offers hydrological and hydrogeological layers, among them the water balance and the river basin atlas, as shapefiles free to download and view in a map viewer, and an indicators page counts 8,263 surface water intakes, 17,447 wells and 166 reservoirs registered in the environmental information system. Access is free and open; no licence is named on the pages read. Caveats: some stations show old readings, the data is operational, and the site is in Spanish. Coverage is Paraguay. It supports flood and drought exposure analysis for water intakes, pumping and river infrastructure; related records are the IMO Iceland hydrometric network and the NEA Georgia hydrometeorological data services.
